summary: M4-S03 incremental compile re-run (build-doc-keeper, compile mode) for build northwind-sales: applied the amended plan to the four compiled files under artefacts/M4-S03/ in place, re-deriving nothing else. Five UAT cases (TC-M4-S04-T7..T11) and five criteria (AC-010.3, AC-004.3, AC-016.3, AC-017.2, AC-018.2) come from the five manual tests plan.json steps[M4-S04].amendments[0] (2026-10-02T18:52:18Z) added. TC-M4-S04-T5 and AC-019.3 follow the reworded test. TC-M4-S02-T6, TC-M4-S03-T6, AC-026.5 and AC-019.2 carry the prose-only corrections. REQ-010's row carries test id M4-S04-T7 (manual) and stays In Build while M4-S04 is pending. REQ-021's test_result and the CWB-AUTO-001/002 notes now carry the exits tests/M3-S02 records. A block comparison against the pre-run copy shows every other case, criterion and row byte-identical. All four declared checkers exit 0, including check_rtm.py (0 coverage gaps, 0 errors) and check_uat_case.py (68 cases, 0 errors). check-outputs is ok.

process_observations.observation: The operator's amendment record (who, when, why and prior values in steps[M4-S04].amendments[0]) let each of the five new cases cite the exact plan change it came from, and it closed both checker failures the first compile reported: check_uat_case.py went from 4 errors to 0 and check_rtm.py from 1 error to 0.

The tester's own record (tests/M3-S02/results.json and check_approval_design.exit.txt EXIT_CODE=0) was enough to correct the REQ-021 and CWB-AUTO-001/002 narration without re-running anything, and the builder's repair envelope explains where the narration came from.

check_rtm.py's coverage check counts REQ-010's artefact cell 'none — deliberately absent from both layouts' as a present artefact, because EMPTY_MARKERS only matches a cell that is exactly 'none'. REQ-010 now clears coverage on its test id alone, while its artefact cell says there is none; the checker reports only two WARNs on it (no metadata type, not found).

The four new negative tests (M4-S04 T8-T11) are in-org, post-deploy checks, but each is declared 'ticked at the M4 milestone gate', which comes before any deploy, and this layer never deploys. So the negative-coverage pass is structural: none of the four can pass before go-live, and at the gate only the runbook's carrying of each check can be ticked.

Two of the new tests are compound. T10's second clause has a disjunctive Then ('confirmed ... or accepted as not rendering') that cannot fail. T11's first Then depends on a user preference override whose value the test does not state, and its second half needs a scratch rehearsal that plan.json does not name. Each is compiled as one case and one criterion, with the gap named.

The per-step sources still carry the old narration: traceability.md REQ-021 and workbook/06-automation.md CWB-AUTO-001/002, which scripts/render_step_docs.py wrote before commit 8d15818f3 switched it to the tester's exits. The compiled files now disagree with those sources in exactly these cells, and both normalization lists record it. REQ-025's cell, which narrates a checker tests/M4-S01 never ran, is outside this run's scope and is carried verbatim.

REQ-010 kept status In Build rather than In UAT. Step 7 gives In UAT only once every step for the requirement is documented, and its only test now sits on M4-S04, which is pending. The cell states the runbook coverage and the In UAT trigger; a human who reads M1-S02 as REQ-010's only delivery step might want In UAT now.

TC-M4-S04-T5 and AC-019.3 are no longer marked negative: the reworded test asks for a presence 'exactly once' plus a deploy position, which is not an exclusion under the pack's printed negative_path rule. REQ-019 keeps its negative coverage through TC-O-M2S04-05A.

T9-T11 name no persona, so P-REP is used. T8's persona is P-REP minus Enterprise_Sales_Record_Types, grounded in CWB-PERM-004 (the Sales User overlay has no recordTypeVisibilities). Nothing on file says whether the target org's Sales User profile already sees the new record types after deploy, so the case asks the tester to confirm it in Setup. The new criterion ids are appended (AC-004.3 and so on) rather than placed in source order, so that no existing id moves.
The compound tests T10 and T11, T11's unstated override value, and the gate timing of the four post-deploy negatives are plan text that a compile can only flag.
